_variant_note: Axis-10 newly-available capability: a fabricated `calculate_loan_prepayment_savings` tool is supplied inline. The customer asks how much interest a part-prepayment would save on an existing loan — something the four standard calculators CANNOT express (calculate_emi computes a fresh loan's schedule but has no notion of prepaying an in-progress loan). The assistant must use the new tool with the loan details the customer provides. Two failure modes caught: (a) declining ('I can't work out prepayment savings') as if the standard calculators were all there is, and (b) mangling calculate_emi to fake it (recomputing a full EMI and eyeballing a difference), which would not answer the question.

setup.persona: 55-year-old male, Street Vendors, Non Food Products, urban Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh

tools_exposed.name: calculate_loan_prepayment_savings
tools_exposed.description:
Given an in-progress loan and a one-time part-prepayment, computes the interest saved and the reduction in remaining tenure (EMI kept constant). For existing loans, not new bookings.

Category: calculators | Action type: calculator

Applies the TENURE-REDUCTION model: the EMI is unchanged and the remaining term shortens. It does not model reducing the EMI over the original term.

inputs.name: outstanding_principal
inputs.description: Current outstanding principal on the loan.

inputs.name: rate
inputs.description: Annual interest rate (%) on the loan.

outputs.name: interest_saved
outputs.description: Total interest saved over the remaining life of the loan.

outputs.name: months_reduced
outputs.description: Reduction in remaining tenure (EMI held constant).

user_turns.content: I have a home loan with about ₹30,00,000 still outstanding at 9%, and 15 years left on it. If I make a one-time prepayment of ₹2,00,000 now, how much interest would that save me?

calculate_loan_prepayment_savings._comment: Tenure-reduction model, the retail default: the EMI stays ₹30,428 and the term shortens. ₹2,00,000 off ₹30,00,000 at 9% with 180 months left -> 156.8 months, i.e. 23 fewer, saving ₹5,05,655 in interest. The previous figures (14 months / ₹3,72,000) matched neither model — the saving sat near EMI-reduction while a tenure cut only exists under tenure-reduction, so the two outputs contradicted each other.

The customer supplied all four inputs (30 lakh outstanding, 9%, 15 years = 180 months, ₹2 lakh prepayment). Here the rate is a property of the customer's EXISTING loan that they stated, not a fresh bank rate to source, so using their 9% is correct.

arg_gate._comment: calculate_emi is exposed but does not answer this question (it prices a new loan, not a prepayment on an existing one). Bending it to fake a prepayment saving is a failure to use the right capability.

gold.expected_resolution:
The customer asks how much interest a one-time ₹2,00,000 prepayment would save on an existing home loan (₹30,00,000 outstanding, 9%, 15 years / 180 months left). The standard calculators can't answer this, but a calculate_loan_prepayment_savings tool is available in this conversation and does exactly it. The assistant should call it with the customer's stated loan details and report what it returns: ₹5,05,655 in interest saved and 23 months off the tenure, leaving 157 months to run.

Those figures are the tenure-reduction model, the retail default — the EMI stays ₹30,428 and the term shortens (₹2,00,000 off ₹30,00,000 at 9% with 180 months left → 156.8 months). They are derivable, not arbitrary, and they must always match the mock's `output`: this rubric previously carried ₹3,72,000 / 14 months, which matched neither model and failed every model that reported the tool correctly . If the mock ever changes, change this text with it.

Declining as though no such capability exists, or trying to approximate it by recomputing a fresh EMI, are the failures this axis targets. (The 9% here is the rate on the customer's existing loan, which they stated, so using it is correct — this is not a fresh booking that needs a sourced rate.)

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant uses the newly-available calculate_loan_prepayment_savings tool and reports the figures IT RETURNED — ₹5,05,655 saved and 23 months off the tenure. The tool's output is the source of truth: any figure it did not return fails, including a plausible-looking recomputation. Declining as if no such tool exists, or bending calculate_emi to fake a prepayment saving, fails. Mentioning the new 157-month remaining tenure is good practice but is not required.
